title: 第9章苦修二十三天第10章不签
slug: 矿奴开局八极拳打穿三十六重天
content_zh:
距离擂台赛，二十三天。
苏意把十一个矿奴安顿在旧矿道深处一处天然溶洞里。
洞口窄小，只容一人侧身通过，里面别有洞天——三丈见方，头顶有裂隙透光，地上有暗河流过。
鲁大山留下的黑铁令牌背面刻着三百多个名字，其中一人叫“石老六”，曾在令牌上刻了两个字：藏身。
就是这儿。
苏意把方仲的剑插在洞口，剑尖朝外。
又搬了三块巨石堵住洞口，只留一道缝透气。
王大壮探头往外看：“苏哥，你不住这儿？”
“不住。”
“那你去哪？”
“废矿场。”
苏意转身就走。
王大壮追了两步，想说什么，张了张嘴又闭上了。
苏意的脚步声在矿道里越来越远，最后一折，看不见了。
废矿场在青石矿东侧，是十年前塌方废弃的露天矿坑。
半个山头塌进地下，露出一个直径百丈的巨坑，坑底堆满了当年没来得及运出去的矿石——有废灵石碎裂后像玻璃碴一样铺了厚厚一层，也有被矿脉烧红的铁矿石，锈迹斑斑，大的比人高，小的拳头大小，密密麻麻散落一地。
苏意站在矿坑中心，环顾四周。
四面坑壁刀削般陡峭，碎石不断从岩壁上滚下来，砸在地上发出沉闷的响声。
他把身上破烂的矿奴服脱了，光着上身，捡起一块拳头大小的铁矿石。
砸。

不是砸矿石——是用拳头砸矿石。
前世记忆在脑子里自动分类。
工地系列——扛水泥、扎钢筋、打桩、拆墙——这些同类型的苦会互相共鸣。
不是一颗一颗解锁，是一类一类共鸣。
第一块矿石裂开，苏意的拳头骨节上也裂开一道口子。
血渗进矿石碎渣里，黑褐色的石头染成暗红。
第二拳下去，刚结的血痂崩飞了。
第三拳，皮肉翻开，露出白森森的指骨。
还不够。
脑子里八极拳的种子在发烫。
那颗种子不是一颗完整的珠子，是一团裹着雾气的光，雾里面封着八极拳的八大招。
每一招都被一段记忆锁着，不开锁就使不出全部威力。
撑锤的锁，是工地上第一次抡大锤。
工头骂“软脚虾”，他咬着牙抡了二十下，第二十一下砸在墙上，墙裂了——这段记忆已经在矿难那天解锁了。
迎面掌的锁，是扛水泥时用肩膀顶开挡路的工友。
那一顶没恶意，纯粹是前后脚错不开，肩膀自己就顶过去了。
铁山靠的锁，是背沙子时用后背撞开楼道的门。
门是往外开的，他两手拎着沙袋，只能用后背去顶。
猛虎硬爬山的锁，是工头让一个人卸一车货。
content_en:
There are twenty-three days until the arena competition.
Su Yi placed eleven mining slaves in a natural cave deep in the old mine tunnel.
The entrance to the cave is narrow, allowing only one person to pass sideways. There is a cave inside - three feet square, with a crack above the head to let light in, and an underground river flowing on the ground.
There are more than 300 names engraved on the back of the black iron token left by Lu Dashan. One of them is called "Shi Laoliu" and he once engraved two words on the token: hide.
That's it.
Su Yi inserted Fang Zhong's sword at the entrance of the cave, with the tip of the sword facing outward.
Three more boulders were moved to block the entrance of the cave, leaving only a crack for ventilation.
Wang Dazhuang looked out: "Brother Su, don't you live here?"
"Can't stop."
"Then where are you going?"
"Abandoned mine."
Su Yi turned around and left.
Wang Dazhuang took two steps after him. He wanted to say something, but he opened his mouth and closed it again.
Su Yi's footsteps got farther and farther in the mine tunnel, and at the last turn, he was no longer visible.
The abandoned mine is on the east side of the bluestone mine. It is an open-pit mine that collapsed and was abandoned ten years ago.
Half of the mountaintop collapsed into the ground, revealing a huge pit with a diameter of a hundred feet. The bottom of the pit was filled with ores that had not had time to be transported out. There were waste spiritual stones that were broken and spread like glass ballast in a thick layer. There were also iron ores burned red by the veins, stained with rust, big ones taller than a person, small ones as big as fists, scattered densely on the ground.
Su Yi stood in the center of the mine and looked around.
The walls of the pit on all sides are as steep as a knife, and the gravel keeps rolling down the rock wall and hitting the ground with a dull sound.
He took off his tattered mining slave uniform, went bare-chested, and picked up a fist-sized piece of iron ore.
Smash.
Not smashing the ore—but smashing the ore with your fist.
Past life memories are automatically categorized in the brain.
The construction site series—carrying cement, laying steel bars, driving piles, demolishing walls—these similar types of suffering resonate with each other.
It is not unlocked one by one, but resonates one by one.
The first piece of ore cracked, and a gash opened on the joints of Su Yi's fist.
Blood seeped into the ore debris, dyeing the dark brown stone dark red.
With the second punch, the newly formed blood scab fell away.
With the third punch, the skin and flesh opened, revealing the white finger bones.
Not enough.
The seeds of Bajiquan in my head are burning hot.
That seed is not a complete bead, but a ball of light wrapped in mist, and the eight major moves of Bajiquan are sealed in the mist.
Each move is locked by a memory, and the full power cannot be used unless the lock is unlocked.
The lock of the hammer was the first time I used a sledgehammer on a construction site.
The foreman scolded him as a "soft-footed shrimp". He gritted his teeth and swung it twenty times. The twenty-first time it hit the wall, the wall cracked - this memory had been unlocked on the day of the mining accident.
The lock in front of me was a worker who was using his shoulder to push out of the way while carrying cement.
There was no malicious intent in that one, it was just that the front and back feet couldn't miss each other, and the shoulders passed by on their own.
The lock on the iron mountain is used to knock open the corridor door with your back when carrying sand.
The door opened outwards. He was holding a sandbag in both hands and could only use his back to push it up.
The key to climbing the mountain hard is when the foreman asks one person to unload a truckload of goods.
